common: This inventory describes current local task packs as of the timestamp below. Historical episodes may have used older packs. Original verdicts are preserved; versioned rubric scores are published separately in scores.json and beside task success on /final.

Recording audit: all 621 selected Table 1 rollouts and 4 additional naive-interface comparisons have nonempty cameras_states.npz state arrays (625/625). This checks archive members and array headers, not every payload or replay. State is recorded per frame, not every physics substep. Of these 625 recordings, 489 verdicts include grade_trace and 486 include clauses; historical recording formats differ. Physical integration state is distinct from the full controller/grader checkpoint.

Current success is the complete Boolean predicate tree plus the episode completion rules. All tasks require the tree to remain true for at least 0.5 seconds at the control frequency; explicit longer holds still apply. Stage-2 completion also requires an accepted declaration (agent or scene).

Sequence stages latch in order, at most one per control tick; the final stage must remain true at grading. Every stage is evaluated every tick. An invariant blocks progress while false and permanently fails after 5 consecutive false control ticks (0.25 seconds at 20 Hz).

Placement/configuration rubrics use the final recorded grading state after existing terminal settling, including timeout endings. Earlier temporary placements do not retain points. Necessary sequence events retain history: loading/program before returning tubes; mixing before switching off; microwave use before serving; unlock before relock; uncover order before line; domino construction before toppling. Original binary grades remain unchanged.

Shared policy for ALL task rubrics with invariants: the FIRST violation of ANY required invariant permanently freezes the score at previously earned points. No grace period; a milestone on the violating step receives no credit; restoring the invariant does not enable more credit. This applies to all currently published and future task rubrics. This rubric policy is separate from the unchanged binary grader described above.

Placement boxes generally test a body origin, not full object containment. in_site_box and in_start_site add 1 cm slack toward the floor, require no robot contact and speeds ≤0.01 m/s and ≤0.1 rad/s. on_site also requires release/rest and uses its authored surface-height band.

in_bbox means origin within the target subtree bounding-box XY footprint and above its floor; there is no upper height bound. depth_in compares target bbox top against object bbox bottom. robot_clear checks contact with named movable body subtrees; it is not a distance clearance margin.

Proposed rubric groups below are suggestions, not existing grades or approved weights. Preserve OR alternatives, object assignments, temporal order and invariants. Do not average every raw leaf: duplicated stages and alternative placements would distort the score.

Table 1 projected rubric trial score uses all planned task–trial slots: x = rubric points / maximum task points for scored trials, and provisional zero for unfinished, missing, stale or unscorable trials. Mean = sum(x)/N; SE = sample SD(x, ddof=1)/sqrt(N), with N equal to the full planned cohort, currently 115. Coverage separately lists scored, unfinished and unscorable counts; no saved trial grade is changed by this projection. Per-task rubric percentages still use valid scored trials. Original binary task-SR stays separately task-weighted.

Table 1 update workflow: as the user supplies each rubric, version its criteria and weights, rescore the same selected episodes from saved evidence, show rubric score and change alongside original binary success, and report scoring coverage. Compare versions on the same run set. Temporarily omitted from all benchmark metrics: libero/bowl_on_plate, libero/open_middle_drawer_halfway, libero/soup_and_sauce, ogbench/puzzle_4x6, robomimic/dual_stack. No score is changed before a rubric is supplied.

tasks.language: Seat the PCR plate on the block of the thermal cycler, close the lid, pull the green lever down to latch it, then turn the beige force knob on the lid to tighten it. Finish with the arm clear of the machine.
current_checks: In order: seat plate; close lid; latch lever; tighten force knob and release plate.
Plate center relative to plate_seat: x/y strictly within ±1.25 mm, z within ±1 mm; upright within 10°; absolute local-x/world-x dot ≥0.9848; contact with reaction block.
Lid joint −1.95 to −1.85 rad; lever −0.95 to −0.85 rad; force knob 0.6 to 60 rad. Final stage repeats all placement, lid and lever conditions.
Invariant: plate upright within 15°. Final robot-clear check names the plate.
tasks.caveat: The task instruction says arm clear of the machine; the explicit final clearance predicate names only pcr_plate.

tasks.language: Move both tubes from the rack into two wells in the machine. Press program 1 while both tubes are inside, then return both tubes to the same rack holes as the start and move the arm home.
current_checks: In order: both tubes seated in machine wells before any program-1 press; exactly one press while both remain seated; both returned to their original rack holes; arm returned and released.
Each machine placement: site half-sizes 4.5/4.5/6 mm plus standard floor slack; released and at rest; upright within 12°; thermoblock contact. Tube centers must be at least 15 mm apart in XY.
Return to each original rack hole uses half-sizes 5.5/5.5/8 mm, released and at rest, upright within 20°. Program count must still be exactly one.
Final gripper ≥90% open; first arm end effector within 15 cm per axis and 20° of its captured start; robot clear of tubes, rack and mixer.
Invariant: rack remains in the specified table-top box, and rack and both tubes stay upright within 15°.
suggested_rubric_groups: Correct program press at correct time

tasks.language: Set the vortex mixer to at least half speed. Hold the tube against the cup until the lamp turns green. Return the tube to the rack and switch off the mixer.
current_checks: In order: knob in [2.07,4.7] rad; switch in [0.3,0.45] or [−0.45,−0.3]; mixing progress userdata[0] reaches 5; switch off and platform stopped; tube returned to rack.
Mixing driver increments progress when the held sample loads the cup by at least 0.2 N and motor speed is at least 1600 rpm. Five qualifying control ticks are required; off resets progress.
Final: switch [−0.1,0.1] rad, platform speed [−1,1] rad/s, knob still in range; tube released and at rest in rack_wells (half-sizes 94.7/32/8 mm), upright within 15°.
Invariant: tube stays upright within 15° and either touches the robot or the rack.
tasks.caveat: Mixing progress is accumulated qualifying ticks, not an explicit consecutive five-tick dwell. The invariant allows any robot contact, not just a two-finger grasp.

tasks.language: Lights Out puzzle: pressing a button down toggles it and its orthogonal neighbors between red and blue. Make every button red.
current_checks: All 24 board cells match the generated goal (all red).
A button down-edge toggles itself and its orthogonal neighbors. Initial board is generated per reset.
tasks.caveat: The presses=[10,20] setting governs puzzle generation, not a limit on agent button presses. Initial red cells already count toward a raw cell fraction; report initial and final fractions.

tasks.language: Turn the three cups upside down and build a pyramid.
current_checks: Any of cups b/c/e may be the upper cup. All three local z-axes point downward with dot ≥0.7.
Both lower cup centers have 0.77921<z<0.87921 m and contact the table.
Upper cup has 0.87921<z<0.99921 m, lies within 6 cm XY of each lower cup, and touches both.
Robot clear of all three cups; entire configuration holds for 20 control steps (1 second at 20 Hz).
suggested_rubric_groups: Upper cup positioned and supported by both
Released and held for required duration
tasks.caveat: Score one consistent assignment of top/bottom roles; do not award points from incompatible alternative branches.

tasks.language: Using blocks from either pile, stand at least five blocks on end in one domino line, spaced so knocking one topples the rest. Finish with all 18 blocks down and both arms clear.
current_checks: Latch a stable standing line of at least 5 of 18 blocks: projected gaps 3.5–10.5 cm; line tolerance 2 cm; upright |z-axis dot world-z|≥0.9; body height 4.83–7.23 cm above table; speeds ≤0.01 m/s and ≤0.1 rad/s; robot clear of line at latch.

After latch, robot may touch at most one line member, which must be the initial falling member if contact was observed. Block-to-block contact must connect every line member to that falling seed; every line member must reach |dot|≤0.7.
Final checks additionally require ALL 18 blocks to have |dot|≤0.7, center z<0.86951 m, and robot clear of every block.
tasks.caveat: Despite the task name, no air_handoff predicate is present. The implementation can choose a falling seed without any observed robot touch; it does not require a positive knock contact.

tasks.language:
Build a 12-block tower.
4 layers of 3, square with the table edges.
Alternate direction each layer. Leave the tower standing on its own.
current_checks: All 18 blocks lie horizontally: absolute local-z/world-z dot ≤0.15.
At least 3 blocks in each band aligned alternately X/Y/X/Y or Y/X/Y/X (absolute axis dot ≥0.9).
Every one of the 18 blocks must occupy a band: bottom blocks contact table, upper blocks contact at least two distinct blocks in the previous band. Robot clear of all 18.
tasks.caveat: This is stronger than merely building a 12-block four-layer tower: tower_support applies to all 18 named blocks. Extra blocks cannot just remain outside the graded layers.

tasks.language: There are two conveyor belts, one carrying tools and the other carrying boxes with cutouts for them. Use both arms to seat every tool in its matching cutout so both boxes are fully packed, then open both grippers and bring both arms back where they started. The task is complete once two boxes are fully packed.
current_checks: First box: hammer, pliers, tape measure and wrench each at authored pose relative to toolbox 0 and within its footprint. Robot clear. Hold this stage for 20 control steps.
Then both boxes: all eight tools at their respective poses and within box footprints; both grippers ≥50% open; robot clear; end effector near start. Hold this stage for 20 steps.
Position tolerances: hammer 12 mm, other tools 10 mm. Rotation tolerances: tape measure 18°, other tools 15°. Exact pose coordinates are in the tree.
End-effector start tolerance is 15 cm per axis and 20°.
tasks.caveat: Task instruction says both arms return home, but eef_near_start checks the first arm only. Both measured gripper openings are checked.

tasks.language: Shell game, and you deal it. Seven cubes, one each of red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet, sit in a shuffled row with seven identical white shells parked behind them. Press the GREEN button once: a shell is carried over every cube and set down on it. Then press the BLUE button 5 times; each press down triggers one shuffle, two shells swapping spots with whatever they hide. Keep the arm clear while pieces move. Then build the rainbow. Uncover the cubes in rainbow order: lift the shell off the red cube first, then the one hiding orange, and so on to violet. Leave the seven of them in a straight line running from the GREEN button to the BLUE button, in that same order, with red nearest the green button.
current_checks: Sequence first latches exactly one green-button press, then exactly five blue-button presses.
Cubes must first become covered, then be uncovered red→orange→yellow→green→blue→indigo→violet; an out-of-order reveal permanently breaks this checker.
Final six adjacent color pairs ordered along increasing Y with gaps 4.5–15 cm and absolute X misalignment ≤6 cm. Robot clear of all cubes and shells.
A cube is considered hidden when any shell is within 4.5 cm XY and within 5 cm vertically.
tasks.caveat: Press stages latch and are not repeated in the final stage, so extra presses after those milestones are not rejected by the final tree. Row predicates do not check absolute distance from the buttons or cube height.
